overview.title: The square that holds the city together
overview.p1: Place el-Hedim is where Meknes orients itself: an open square facing Bab Mansour, edged by cafés, shops and the flow into the medina. It is less theatrical than Jemaa el-Fnaa and more practical — a place to meet, pause and watch the gate change colour.
overview.p2: Come once in the morning for space and soft light, and again toward evening when the square fills and the monument glows. Street sellers and terraces appear; the atmosphere stays local rather than staged for coaches alone.
overview.p3: Use the square as your base for the first day: gate, medina entry, museum, then return for tea. You will cross it more than once, and that repetition is part of understanding Meknes’s rhythm.

q1.question: Is Place el-Hedim safe at night?
q1.answer: It is generally busy and fine in the evening. Use normal city sense, keep valuables close, and take a taxi if you are returning late to Ville Nouvelle.

q2.question: Do I need a ticket?
q2.answer: No. The square is public space.

q3.question: How long to spend?
q3.answer: Thirty minutes for a first look, or longer if you sit for tea and return at sunset.

q4.question: Is it good with children?
q4.answer: Yes — open space to move, but watch scooters and keep them close in crowds.

q5.question: Where do I go next?
q5.answer: Bab Mansour is on the square. The medina and Dar Jamai sit a short walk away.

food.title: Tea and snacks on the square
food.p1: Terraces around Place el-Hedim are made for a break with the gate in view. Meals are simple; for richer cooking, walk into the medina or book a riad table.
food.p2: Evening is the liveliest time for a casual bite without planning a full restaurant stop.
food.li1: Mint tea with a view of Bab Mansour
food.li2: Nuts, olives and biscuits from edge stalls
food.li3: Grilled snacks when the square fills after dark
food.li4: Water and shade at midday in summer
food.li5: Save a proper tagine for a medina or riad kitchen

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Place el-Hedim

1.title: Use it as a compass, not only a photo stop
1.desc: Note the position of Bab Mansour, the medina entrances and the direction of Ville Nouvelle. Returning to the square between visits keeps you oriented without maps every five minutes.

2.title: Morning calm, evening energy
2.desc: Early hours are best for photos without crowds. After late afternoon the square becomes social — better for atmosphere than for empty architectural shots.

3.title: Agree prices before you sit
3.desc: Some terraces quote loosely for drinks. Confirm the price of tea or juice before you order, and move on if the approach feels pushy.
